title: Self-Care
subtitle: Self-care 是一個很廣的概念。 它可以指日常照顧自己、促進身心健康的習慣、慢性病自我管理、基本個人護理、健康生活規律，甚至保留休息和恢復的個人時間。因此替換前要先判斷是在說
description: Self-care 是一個很廣的概念。 它可以指日常照顧自己、促進身心健康的習慣、慢性病自我管理、基本個人護理、健康生活規律，甚至保留休息和恢復的個人時間。因此替換前要先判斷是在說 general wellbeing, structured health management, personal hygiene, daily routines, emotional nurturing, 還是 relaxation time。

words.meaning: 照顧自己；照料自己的需要
words.example: After a demanding week, she made more time for looking after herself.
words.exampleZh: 經過忙碌的一週後，她花更多時間照顧自己。

exercises.original: She has become more deliberate about self-care during stressful periods.
exercises.zh: 在壓力大的時期，她更刻意照顧自己。
exercises.upgrade: She has become more deliberate about looking after herself during stressful periods.

options.explanation: Looking after oneself ✓ — means taking practical care of one's own physical, emotional and everyday needs. Here, the sentence simply means taking practical care of one's own needs. That makes Looking after oneself the most precise reformulation of this particular sense of self-care.

Personal well-being practices — means concrete habits or activities intended to support physical, mental or emotional wellbeing. This points to concrete wellbeing activities and is less suitable when the sentence is about broad self-care, clinical self-management, or basic personal care. The decisive clue is that the sentence simply means taking practical care of one's own needs.

Healthy routines — means regular repeated habits that support physical and mental health. This requires repeated daily habits; it is too narrow for one-off support, emotional self-kindness, or personal-care tasks. The decisive clue is that the sentence simply means taking practical care of one's own needs.

Selfishness — means prioritising oneself without due regard for others and is not the same as self-care. This changes the meaning negatively: caring for one's needs does not imply disregarding other people. The decisive clue is that the sentence simply means taking practical care of one's own needs.

Leisure — means free time or recreational activity and does not necessarily have a self-care purpose. Leisure may help wellbeing, but free time is not automatically purposeful self-care. The decisive clue is that the sentence simply means taking practical care of one's own needs.

Pampering — means giving oneself pleasurable or indulgent treatment and is only one possible form of self-care. This suggests indulgence or treats and is much narrower than the broader health and wellbeing concept. The decisive clue is that the sentence simply means taking practical care of one's own needs.

exercises.upgrade: During busy periods, healthy routines often start with regular meals and sleep.

options.explanation: Wellness practices — means activities intended to promote overall health and wellbeing. This works for lifestyle activities, but not for basic hygiene or structured condition management. The decisive clue is that the sentence identifies recurring daily habits.

Personal well-being practices — means concrete habits or activities intended to support physical, mental or emotional wellbeing. This points to concrete wellbeing activities and is less suitable when the sentence is about broad self-care, clinical self-management, or basic personal care. The decisive clue is that the sentence identifies recurring daily habits.

Rest — means stopping activity to recover and is only one component of self-care. Rest is one component of self-care, not the whole concept. The decisive clue is that the sentence identifies recurring daily habits.

Leisure — means free time or recreational activity and does not necessarily have a self-care purpose. Leisure may help wellbeing, but free time is not automatically purposeful self-care. The decisive clue is that the sentence identifies recurring daily habits.

Pampering — means giving oneself pleasurable or indulgent treatment and is only one possible form of self-care. This suggests indulgence or treats and is much narrower than the broader health and wellbeing concept. The decisive clue is that the sentence identifies recurring daily habits.

Healthy routines ✓ — means regular repeated habits that support physical and mental health. Here, the sentence identifies recurring daily habits. That makes Healthy routines the most precise reformulation of this particular sense of self-care.

words.example: Quiet time can be an important form of self-nurturing.

words.meaning: 屬於自己的時間；獨處放鬆時間
words.example: She protects an hour of me-time at the end of each week.
words.exampleZh: 她每週末都會保留一小時屬於自己的放鬆時間。

exercises.original: She schedules Sunday afternoon for self-care and relaxation.
exercises.zh: 她安排星期日下午作為屬於自己的放鬆時間。
exercises.upgrade: She schedules Sunday afternoon for me-time and relaxation.

options.explanation: Me-time ✓ — means informal personal time set aside for rest, relaxation or enjoyable activities. Here, the sentence is specifically about reserving personal leisure time. That makes Me-time the most precise reformulation of this particular sense of self-care.

Healthy routines — means regular repeated habits that support physical and mental health. This requires repeated daily habits; it is too narrow for one-off support, emotional self-kindness, or personal-care tasks. The decisive clue is that the sentence is specifically about reserving personal leisure time.

Personal care — means basic daily care such as washing, dressing, grooming and hygiene. This is restricted to hygiene and activities of daily living, so it is too narrow outside care-service contexts. The decisive clue is that the sentence is specifically about reserving personal leisure time.

Wellness practices — means activities intended to promote overall health and wellbeing. This works for lifestyle activities, but not for basic hygiene or structured condition management. The decisive clue is that the sentence is specifically about reserving personal leisure time.

Rest — means stopping activity to recover and is only one component of self-care. Rest is one component of self-care, not the whole concept. The decisive clue is that the sentence is specifically about reserving personal leisure time.

exercises.upgrade: A little me-time after a busy week can help her recharge.

falseSynonyms.zh: 自私 ≠ self-care self-care 是合理照顧自身需要；selfishness 是不顧他人需要。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Self-care and selfishness are not the same.

falseSynonyms.zh: 寵愛自己 ≠ 所有 self-care pampering 只是享受型活動，self-care 可包括睡眠、求助、治療和設立界線。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Pampering is only one possible form.

falseSynonyms.zh: 休閒 ≠ self-care 休閒可以促進 wellbeing，但並非所有 leisure 都有自我照顧目的。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Leisure is broader and purpose-neutral.

falseSynonyms.zh: 只在日常自理 sense 接近 personal care 偏洗澡、穿衣、梳洗等基本生活照顧。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Personal care is narrower.

falseSynonyms.zh: 只在系統性管理 sense 接近 self-management 常涉及健康狀況、行為、藥物或生活管理。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Self-management is more structured.

falseSynonyms.zh: 健康狀態／概念 ≠ self-care action wellness 是狀態或整體理念；self-care 是實際行動／做法。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Wellness is an outcome or broader concept.

falseSynonyms.zh: 休息 ≠ 所有 self-care rest 是 self-care 的一種做法，但範圍太窄。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Rest is one component.

falseSynonyms.zh: 詞義與結構陷阱 care 可指照顧他人；self-care 明確指照顧自己。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON The reflexive meaning matters.
